Alex W: Quick check — clarifying the streaming delta contract for tool/function calls. If args for a func_call arrive across multiple delta events and another func_call starts before the first finishes (interleaved), what do we guarantee to clients?

Alex W: Example (very simplified):
```json
{ "event": "tool_call", "call_id": "call-1", "chunk": "{\"q\": \"part1\"}" }
{ "event": "tool_call", "call_id": "call-2", "chunk": "{\"q\": \"other\"}" }
{ "event": "tool_call", "call_id": "call-1", "chunk": "{\"q\": \"part2\"}" }
```

Caroline: Short answer: we must guarantee deterministic reassembly by call_id. Clients should be able to reassemble chunks belonging to the same call_id in the order they were emitted and only treat the call as complete when a terminal flag or final chunk is seen.

Ben K: Agree. We should explicitly define fields in the delta envelope: `call_id`, `chunk_index` (optional but helpful), `is_final` (boolean), and `event_type` (tool_call_start/tool_call_chunk/tool_call_end). Clients can fall back to sequence order if chunk_index missing.

InfraBot: FYI: canary deploy queued — will run streaming-toolargs test suite against staging after schema PR lands.

Matt R: Question: are we comfortable with allowing "partial JSON" in chunks (i.e., chunks that aren't valid JSON until concatenated)? SDKs will need to buffer and not attempt to parse until final.

Caroline: Yes. Runtime may stream raw bytes. Document: "chunks are opaque until reassembled; only final concatenated bytes are validated and parsed." Add explicit interoperable behavior for older clients that don't understand streaming chunks.

Sara: Proposal: add `chunk_index` + `final` boolean. Also add `fallback_single_message` flag server-side: if client sets it (old clients), runtime will collapse into a single delta when feasible.

Alex W: Good. I'll open a docs PR with the recommended envelope and pseudocode for client reassembly. Also adding a small harness that simulates interleaved calls. Assigning: @Caroline to update schema, @Ben K to add SDK tests, @Alice M to add backwards-compat notes.

Ben K: I'll add tests for these cases: 1) contiguous chunks, 2) interleaved calls, 3) missing final chunk (timeout policy), 4) final chunk out of order but with chunk_index present.

Alice M: Note on backward compatibility: if no streaming is used, the runtime will still emit a single completed tool_call delta. Add a compatibility example in the docs that shows the old single-delta payload and the new streaming envelope.

Alex W: Also small ops question — what timeout for reassembly? Proposal: 30s by default, configurable per-tenant. If final not seen in timeout, emit an error event on the stream referencing call_id.

Caroline: +1 to configurable timeout. Document default and recommended values. Also mark this as a potential compatibility hazard in the migration guide.

InfraBot: canary run scheduled: streaming-toolargs suite -> staging -> results at /ci/canaries/streaming-toolargs/4456789012

Matt R: Cool. I'll check SDK patch for buffering behavior. If anyone wants to ride along on the canary run, ping me.

Alex W: Thanks all — I'll drop the PR links here when ready. :thumbsup:
